title: Heavily Seasoned Korean Fish Korean Fried Chicken
description: A fresh and juicy Korean dish featuring fish, inspired by the flavors of Gyeonggi province, adapted to be fodmap-friendly.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together cornstarch, Korean chili flakes, gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger.
Add the fish pieces to the bowl and toss to coat evenly.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours.
Remove the fish from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for 15 minutes.
In a shallow dish, mix together egg whites and a pinch of salt.
In a separate shallow dish, place the panko breadcrumbs.
Dip each piece of fish into the egg whites, coating lightly, then roll in the panko breadcrumbs to coat evenly.
Heat about 1/2-inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C).
Fry the breaded fish pieces in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per batch.
Transfer the fried fish to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the korean fried chicken hot with green onions, toasted sesame seeds, and a side of crushed ice.
Garnish with additional green onions and sesame seeds, if desired.
